findings: The complete November canonical capture identifies the topic and routes to the iOS, Android and React Native variants. It omits every implementation body; the corresponding April 22, 2026 sections are located at old raw 14–16, 170–172 and 356–358 despite the older filename. New raw 1–15 and old raw 568–572 separate the new links from the old code fence joined on diff line 573.

The April guide requires a Stripe account and an existing EmbeddedPaymentElement integration before setting up a Dashboard custom method with display name/logo and `cpmt_` type ID. When a selected custom method is confirmed, the handler receives it and any collected billing details, the merchant uses its processor to complete the payment outside Stripe, and the handler returns or reports the outcome to the UI. Optional server-side Stripe reporting follows external processing (old raw 8–38, 60–90, 242–273, 416–485 and 520–572).

The summary shows reporting and platform declarations but omits the external provider call and its outcome as the gating step. Its React Native stub always calls `Completed` without explaining the old sample’s demonstration-only alert. Its opening comparison generalizes an iOS result type, and its report call lacks dated API and identifier boundaries (source 13–23, 25–87; old raw 60–90, 116–168, 193–249 and 416–485).
historical_claims_to_preserve: Date the account, existing embedded integration, Dashboard display name/logo, Dashboard `cpmt_` type ID, external provider finalization and merchant PSP agreement/applicable law responsibility to the April 22, 2026 guide (old raw 8–38, 174–193, 360–379).

Date and distinguish iOS `@_spi(CustomPaymentMethodsBeta)` import of `StripePaymentSheet` and async `EmbeddedPaymentElementResult` from the separate PaymentSheet/FlowController guide’s `PaymentSheetResult`. The embedded Swift prose says `failure(error:)` whereas its concrete code returns `.failed(error:)`. Android wires `ConfirmCustomPaymentMethodCallback` and sends `CustomPaymentMethodResult` through `CustomPaymentMethodResultHandler`, including canceled when it might exit unconfirmed. React Native calls the provided `resultHandler` with `Completed`, `Canceled`, or `Failed`; the example uses a demonstration alert and the old prose says a supplied failure message is displayed (old raw 37–90, 193–273, 378–485; related raw/stripe-inapp-custom-payment-methods-2025.md:35-57).

Date embedded configuration of custom methods after Stripe-supported methods by default, explicit `paymentMethodOrder`, and default-off billing detail collection with opt-in `disableBillingDetailCollection = false`. The iOS/Android text links `billingDetailsCollectionConfiguration`; React Native links `defaultBillingDetails` and still uses the opt-in flag (old raw 92–108, 275–294 and 487–511).

Keep optional server-side recording distinct from external processing. The dated samples create a `PaymentMethod` of `type: 'custom'` whose `custom.type` is the Dashboard type ID, pass the resulting `paymentMethod.id` to `paymentRecords.reportPayment`, give the external processor payment reference separately and illustrate `outcome: 'guaranteed'` for a successful externally processed payment. The samples use `2026-03-25.dahlia; invoice_partial_payments_beta=v3`; the April sample alone does not establish current availability or a universal version requirement (old raw 116–168, 302–354 and 520–572).
conflicts: Source lines 77–87 call `Completed` unconditionally. The April React Native sample calls `Completed`, `Failed` or `Canceled` in a demonstration alert, after telling the implementer to complete payment with the provider; iOS and Android examples deliberately report failure (old raw 62–87, 244–270, 418–485). Expose in the summary that handler completion conveys the provider outcome and an example or SDK callback does not prove an external payment or settlement.

Source line 13 and in-app concept line 100 generalize `EmbeddedPaymentElementResult`; the archived embedded Swift handler returns that type, Android passes `CustomPaymentMethodResult` while separately observing `EmbeddedPaymentElement.Result`, and React Native calls a supplied result handler. The generic Stripe Custom Payment Methods concept’s lines 119–127 list `PaymentSheetResult` under broad mobile guidance; keep that iOS signature scoped to PaymentSheet/FlowController and add an embedded route (old raw 37–90, 193–270, 378–485; raw/stripe-inapp-custom-payment-methods-2025.md:35-57). The same Dashboard setup is corroborated by the related PaymentSheet route’s raw lines 18–33.

Source line 22 omits that optional PaymentRecord calls report an external result and use the created PaymentMethod ID separately from the `cpmt_` type and external processor reference. The source line 28 import wording and line 22 reporting shorthand should be scoped to the dated Swift beta/recording examples, with the exact sample version where needed, and without equating `guaranteed` with a new Stripe charge or settlement (old raw 37–40, 116–168, 520–572).
unresolved_questions: The November selector does not establish linked variant contents, current embedded SDK availability or access to the sample’s API version/feature flag. Neither capture verifies a live third-party execution or a successful Stripe report.

findings: Route both dated snapshots and state prerequisites and merchant responsibilities. Move the outside-Stripe processor completion and observed result ahead of the iOS/Android/React Native handler examples, and mark the React Native demonstration as such (source 6–23 and 75–87; old raw 8–38, 416–485; new raw 5–15).

Scope `EmbeddedPaymentElementResult` to the Swift handler, preserve the archived prose/code spelling difference and Android cancellation handoff, and retain the native versus React Native billing/order qualifications. Adjust reciprocal routes to distinguish the embedded UI from PaymentSheet/FlowController (source 13–21 and 25–86; old raw 37–108, 193–294, 378–511; in-app concept 99–100 and custom-method concept 119–127).

Qualify optional server reporting with the dated sample version and separate Dashboard `cpmt_` type ID, generated Stripe PaymentMethod ID and external processor reference. Report the external result rather than implying Stripe charges or guarantees payment from `reportPayment` (source 22; old raw 116–168, 302–354 and 520–572).
conflicts: React Native example in source 78–86 returns success unconditionally. Old raw 418–485 demonstrates outcome choices and requires the merchant to complete externally.

The source-wide `EmbeddedPaymentElementResult` contrast in line 13 and in-app concept line 100 needs an iOS scope, while the broad custom-method concept lines 119–127 need the separate embedded route. Android and React Native use differently named result channels (old raw 37–90, 193–273, 378–485).
Source 22 leaves a reader unable to distinguish provider processing from the optional reporting call, its three identifiers and its sample version (old raw 116–168 and 520–572).
source_assessments.reason: The new raw is navigation only. The existing summary needs corrections for the external completion boundary, conditional callbacks, platform scope and optional reporting so readers can select the right client API and avoid mistaking a demo outcome or PaymentRecord for processing.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/embedded-custom-payment-methods, new raw lines 5-15 identify the topic and route to iOS, Android and React Native variants without their bodies. The April 22, 2026 guide requires a Stripe account and an existing embedded integration, then a Dashboard display name/logo and a custom method type identified by `cpmt_` (old raw lines 8-38, 174-193 and 360-379). Confirmation with that method selected invokes a handler with any collected billing details. The merchant completes the transaction through its processor outside Stripe and then reports the observed result to the UI. iOS returns `EmbeddedPaymentElementResult`; Android sends `CustomPaymentMethodResult` through its result handler even when exiting unconfirmed, as canceled; React Native invokes the supplied `resultHandler` with Completed, Canceled or Failed (old raw lines 60-90, 242-273 and 416-485). Optional server reporting uses a separately created Stripe PaymentMethod ID and external processor reference (old raw lines 116-168). source-stripe-inapp-embedded-custom-payment-methods.md captures core configuration but needs to scope the iOS signature and replace its unexplained immediate React Native success with the external outcome boundary.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/embedded-custom-payment-methods, new raw lines 5-15 show a presentation change to variant navigation. The April 22, 2026 bodies represented in old raw lines 14-38, 170-193 and 356-379 remain the dated evidence for the integration. In source-stripe-inapp-embedded-custom-payment-methods.md and the reciprocal in-app and custom-method concept routes, scope `EmbeddedPaymentElementResult` to the Swift embedded handler and keep the distinct Android callback/canceled result and React Native result handler. The Swift sample imports the beta SPI and returns `.failed(error:)` even though nearby prose says `failure(error:)`. React Native's alert choices demonstrate results and do not process a payment (old raw lines 37-90, 193-273 and 416-485). Keep default ordering after Stripe-supported methods and billing collection disabled until opt-in (old raw lines 92-108, 275-294 and 487-511). The April optional server report sample uses `2026-03-25.dahlia; invoice_partial_payments_beta=v3` and distinguishes the Dashboard type ID, generated Stripe PaymentMethod ID and external processor payment reference (old raw lines 116-168 and 520-572). A `guaranteed` reporting example conveys an external outcome, and the selector supplies no evidence of current access, Stripe payment processing, settlement or live success.
